item.title: Jewish Film Festival: The Last Twins — Tue Oct 13, 1:00 PM
item.description:
The Last Twins is the never-before-told story of an unsung hero of the Holocaust, Erno “Zvi” Spiegel, who risked everything to save dozens of young twins from almost certain death at Auschwitz. Under the shadow of Dr. Josef Mengele’s horrific experiments, Spiegel used his courage, compassion, and ingenuity to shield the most vulnerable—the sets of twins targeted for brutal medical experimentation. Mengele put Spiegel in charge of the young boys, but Spiegel used his position to protect and comfort the children, all of whom had been torn from their families and subjected to inhumane tests under the constant threat of extermination.
Source: Sebastopol Chamber of Commerce, North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Sebastopol Calendar

The weekend continues with unique events including Cheese, Chocolate & Cheers!, A Taste of Stories, Cattle, Cabernet & Country, Taste YOUR Terroir, A New Orleans Afternoon, Barrels & Bootleggers, Bubbles, Brunch & B-Sides, and more. item.title: Ellie James Music — Fri Oct 16, 6:00 PM — Baldassari Wine Lounge
item.description:
Your new favorite song is just around the corner. Enter the world of singer-songwriter and producer Ellie James, and treat yourself to a show unlike any you've ever seen. Stylistically unique and captivating, Ellie James mixes lush indie-pop sounds with the style and edge of her rock ’n’ roll background. Her music is both genuine and dance-inducing, as she uses real instruments and electronic production to weave musical stories all her own. Ellie has been performing professionally all over the world for more than 10 years, most recently opening up for Grammy-winning artist Colbie Caillat, and playing to electric audiences at Hollywood’s famous Viper Room and San Francisco’s Cafe du Nord. With the release of her much-anticipated sophomore EP “Favorite Stranger” and a nearly sold-out headlining show at Hopmonk, Ellie shows no signs of stopping with a year ahead full of new shows, new merch, and new music.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Using AI to Bring Your Presentation to Life — Sat Oct 17, 12:30 PM
item.description:
The Sonoma County Genealogical Society Presents
**Using AI to Bring Your Presentation to Life**
**Presented by Jane Pritchard**
Jane will present the slide show she created for the Santa Rosa Chapter of the DAR honoring her Revolutionary War patriot, Margaret Eskridge Kenner, who supported Revolutionary troops with food and supplies. Along the way she taught herself to use AI assistants Claude and Nano Banana, to speed up research and to build both the PowerPoint and a companion PDF. She will walk through the simple, practical ways she used AI — and where it fell short so members can try the same approach with their own ancestors.
Jane began serious family research in 2021, during the pandemic, and has since taken many genealogy classes through Santa Rosa Junior College. She was surprised to discover that her ancestors played a part in the founding of this country — a history her family had never known. item.title: Reuse in Art, Reuse in Life: A Conversation Between Ali Gass and Phoebe Schenker — Sun Oct 18, 3:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Alison Gass, Founding Executive Director of the ICA San Francisco, and Phoebe Schenker, Executive Director of Reuse Alliance, for a wide-ranging conversation about reuse in contemporary and historical art and why it is more relevant than ever.
The discussion will explore the many ways artists have engaged with reuse, from incorporating found and reclaimed materials to making reuse itself a central subject of their work. Together, Gass and Schenker will consider how reuse connects to broader cultural conversations about creativity, sustainability, consumption, and value, while also exploring how reuse can become a creative practice in our own everyday lives.
